text:
Kris Letang is 39, in his 21st season with the only team he's played for, and he's still playing 20 minutes a night. The results are better than his line suggests. Pittsburgh has 56.1% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, five points better than without him, and his eight points in 18 games come mostly from setting others up, which is what he's always done best.

His own shooting is the weak spot. One goal on 34 shots, and our wins-added numbers have him near the very bottom of the league, mostly because his shots haven't gone in at big moments. The Penguins have also scored about four more goals than expected with him out there, so his assists are running a touch warm.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a playmaker last season, 93rd percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists, even though Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level overall. The three-time Cup winner and Masterton winner isn't the player he was. He's still useful. Our range has him around 35 points.
headline: Kris Letang is still running Pittsburgh's play
